references.text: The parallel passage in the Sermon on the Mount where Jesus says exactly the same thing: "For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also" ([ref:Matt 6:21|Matthew 6:21]). This is the closest parallel to Luke 12:34.

The immediate context in Matthew's version, where Jesus warns against storing up treasures on earth and encourages storing up treasures in heaven ([ref:Matt 6:19-20|Matthew 6:19-20]), which corresponds to Luke 12:33.

"Guard your heart above all else, for it is the source of life." ([ref:Prov 4:23|Proverbs 4:23]). Proverbs emphasizes the central importance of the heart, something Jesus builds upon when he links the heart to what one values most.
"Give me your heart, my son" ([ref:Prov 23:26|Proverbs 23:26]). Wisdom asks for the wholehearted devotion of the heart, just as Jesus teaches that the heart follows after what is set highest.

Paul urges believers: "Set your minds on things above … Let your mind be focused on what is above, not on what is on earth" ([ref:Col 3:1-2|Colossians 3:1-2]). This expands on Jesus' teaching that the heart should be directed toward heavenly treasure.

Paul contrasts those who "set their minds on earthly things" with those whose citizenship is in heaven ([ref:Phil 3:19-20|Philippians 3:19-20]). This illustrates the principle in Luke 12:34 — the heart follows the treasure.

The immediate context where Jesus says: "Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Provide yourselves with purses that do not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in heaven" ([ref:Luk 12:33|Luke 12:33]). Verse 34 is the reason for this call.

James warns: "Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God?" ([ref:Jas 4:4|James 4:4]). A divided heart between God and the world is impossible, which supports Jesus' point that the heart must choose its treasure.

"No one can serve two masters" ([ref:Matt 6:24|Matthew 6:24]). In the same context as Matt 6:21, Jesus teaches that the heart cannot be divided between God and mammon — the treasure determines loyalty.

John warns against loving the world or what is in it, for "whoever loves the world does not have the love of the Father in them" ([ref:1 John 2:15-17|1 John 2:15-17]). The direction of the heart — toward earthly or heavenly treasure — is decisive.
